# Corpus programs where `-target arm64-linux -backend ssa` behaves DIFFERENTLY
# from the shipping flat-IR arm64 backend. Read by
# internal/e2e/arm64_ssa_differential_test.go; format is `<path>  <reason>`.
#
# Exact in BOTH directions. A listed program that starts AGREEING fails the
# test, and so does one that stops compiling under either backend — a row is a
# claim about an answer, and a program that no longer produces one cannot
# support it. Delete the row; do not let it sit here unverified.
#
# These are bugs in the proving ground, not sanctioned behaviour.
# docs/SSA-DECISION.md holds the native SSA backends to "byte-identical-in-
# behaviour to the flat-IR backends ... across their covered subset", and every
# program below is inside that subset: it compiled clean and then behaved
# differently. A program the SSA backend REFUSES does not belong here — that is
# the documented coverage endpoint and the test counts it separately.
#

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Wrong answers, no crash (4 rows)
#
# Exit codes alone would not have found these: three of the four
# exit 0 or 1 and print the wrong thing.
#
# The first three are one defect, reduced 2026-08-22: an f32 stored into a
# multi-slot aggregate lands only in the LAST slot, and every earlier slot keeps
# whatever was there (zero, or a denormal from a half-width store).
#
#   enum Sh { Tri(f32, f32) }  Tri(4, 2.5) then matched: flat gives b=4 h=2.5,
#                              arm64ssa gives b=0 h=2.5
#   var xs: f32[] = [1,2,3]    flat gives 1,2,3; arm64ssa gives 0,0,3
#   enum Sh { One(f32) }       agrees — a single-slot payload is fine
#
# The fourth is unrelated: an f64 NaN payload.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

examples/tests/float_array_strict_sort_test.fern  f32 array element reads back as a denormal — case 6 sees 0e-44 at index 1 where the flat backend sees 2 (multi-slot f32 store, see header)
examples/tests/assert_at_wider_test.fern  f32 array element reads back as 0 — assert_at_f32 case 12 sees 0 at index 0 where the flat backend sees 1 (multi-slot f32 store, see header)
examples/wasm/shape_area.fern  first f32 field of a two-field variant payload reads back as 0 — Triangle(4,2.5) takes the "non-positive triangle dim" guard instead of printing area 5 (multi-slot f32 store, see header)
examples/proposals/float_bits.fern  f64 signalling-NaN payload is quieted — the sNaN mantissa arrives as 2251799813685248 (the quiet bit) instead of 1, so the two NaN payloads decode identically
